newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to lower share trade risk for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to lower share trade risk for foreigners.

text.p: Latvia's central securities depository (LCD) on Thursday said it wanted to decrease the risk for foreign investors active on its stock market by allowing them to have securities accounts at the depository itself.
Previously, foreign investors could only hold shares in commercial banks' or brokers' securities accounts.
"Big foreign investors during meetings have enquired how the risk of investing in Latvia can be decreased," the central depository said in a statement.
"To improve this situation, the LCD is working on a procedure that will allow foreign investors to open securities directly with the LCD," it added.

Latvia and the other Baltic stock markets have increasingly attracted foreign investors although some are still worried over the situation of the banks in these countries after recent bank sector crises.
Transactions in securities will still have to be carried out through a licenced local dealer but the shares can be kept at separate accounts at the depository.
